clue.text: The uncertainty of coming in by river

parts.note: per is Latin-derived 'by', as in 'per post'
an advent is an arrival or coming in
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the doubts of arriving somewhere by river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The uncertainty' reads as a sentence opener, but the noun alone is the definition, as in the phrase 'beyond peradventure'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an archaic noun the word means doubt, the chance that something may not be so.

clue.text: Nationalist Irishman accommodating the musketeers, possibly?

indicators.note: one name holding another inside it, as a host accommodates a guest

parts.note: Pat is a stock nickname for an Irishman
the Three Musketeers were a threesome, so a trio is one example

explanation.surface: An Irish nationalist puts up Dumas's famous swordsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is a person devoted to their country, which a nationalist also is.

clue.text: In bistro, a steel pan is used

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words bistro, a steel

explanation.surface: In a small restaurant, a steel frying pan is in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking vessel, but it is the verb meaning to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play is to criticise it severely, the same sense as savaging it in a review.

clue.text: Rising Edwardian youth put on fur to give judgement

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a Teddy boy or Ted was a 1950s youth in Edwardian-style dress
ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: A Teddy boy dons a fur before passing a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edwardian youth' sounds like a young man of 1901-10, but means a 1950s Teddy boy; 'Rising' flips him in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine a case is to decide it, which is what a judge does on giving a ruling.

clue.text: Noble king has leader relegated to lowest position

indicators.text: has leader relegated to lowest position
indicators.note: the opening letter of the king's name is sent down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A monarch sees his chief demoted to the bottom rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, one rank of the nobility.

clue.text: One betrayer's daughter taken in by another

indicators.note: one word is held inside another, as a guest is taken in

parts.note: another betrayer, so a traitor

explanation.surface: One turncoat's daughter is deceived by a second turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to the definition: another betrayer is TRAITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditor was an early Christian who surrendered scriptures to persecutors, hence a betrayer.

clue.text: Instrument about to be abandoned by the first Mrs de Winter

indicators.note: the short word for about is dropped from the name

parts.note: Rebecca, in Daphne du Maurier's novel, is Maxim de Winter's dead first wife
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is about to be left behind by a famous fictional wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to', but it gives CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, an ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: Agree to commander serving a sentence, say

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a convict serving a sentence is inside, in jail

explanation.surface: Someone tells their commanding officer they are doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that coincide match each other, so they concur.

clue.text: River warrior

explanation.surface: A fighter on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American river; the Amazons were mythical women fighters.

clue.text: Where the rejection of a dessert stirred up a riot?

indicators.note: rejection sends the word back, read right to left

parts.note: a tart is a sweet pastry dessert

indicators.note: a riot stirred up has its letters thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Diners rejecting a pudding sparks a restaurant riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rejection of' turns TART into TRAT; 'stirred up' shuffles A RIOT into TORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an Italian restaurant, a place where such a scene could happen.

clue.text: Plant originally replaced during a prosperous period

indicators.note: one letter comes in the middle of the period

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A plant is changed out during good economic times.
explanation.definitionFit: Broom is a yellow-flowered shrub of heaths.

clue.text: Detain a doctor in New York, perhaps

definitions.text: a doctor in New York, perhaps

explanation.surface: A New York physician is held back.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine, as in wartime; in the US a hospital junior doctor is called by the same word.

clue.text: They may be kept in their place by a clip on the nose!

definitions.text: They may be kept in their place by a clip on the nose!

parts.words: They may be kept in their place by a clip on the nose!
parts.note: a clip on the nose sounds like a blow, but describes spectacles held on with a spring pinch and no arms

explanation.surface: Unruly people are put in their place with a punch on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: These are old-fashioned spectacles that grip the bridge of the nose with a spring.

clue.text: Alarm caused by rumour of poison

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard, so the word for poison is judged by its sound

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: Gossip about a poisoning sets off panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Star with house in Italy is a rake

parts.note: casa is Italian for house
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity with an Italian villa is a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces, the house coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova, the Venetian seducer, gave his name to any womaniser.

clue.text: Engineers withdrawing motion demanding an explanation

indicators.note: the engineers are taken out of the formal motion

parts.note: a resolution is a motion put to a meeting
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Army engineers drop a motion that called for answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is the answer to a problem, which explains it.

clue.text: Endless muddle in gun case

indicators.note: the letters of in gun case are muddled up

explanation.surface: A gun case is in permanent disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing never stops, so it has no end.

clue.text: Negotiator given certificate before beginning of trial

indicators.note: the certificate comes before the next piece

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification

indicators.note: beginning of means only the opening letter of trial

explanation.surface: A negotiator is awarded a qualification ahead of a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat conducts negotiations between states.

clue.text: Extremely morose sergeant-major, gradually dominating the will

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of morose

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story by F. W. Farrar, so little by little, gradually, gives Eric

explanation.surface: A gloomy sergeant-major slowly imposes his will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gradually' is a crossword joke: the novel's subtitle 'Little by Little' links ERIC with gradualness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmeric means hypnotic, holding another's mind in thrall as Mesmer claimed to.

clue.text: Two maidens displaying ill-will?

parts.note: M is maiden, a scoreless over in cricket
Alice is a maiden, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pair of young women show spite.
explanation.walkthrough: The two maidens are of different kinds: a cricket maiden over (M) and a girl, ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spiteful intent to harm, the same as bad feeling toward someone.

clue.text: Go away without key? What a hoot!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the departure word goes around

parts.note: scram! means go away
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave without their key finds it hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: SCRAM goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is called a scream or a hoot.

clue.text: Island admitting a non-professional Asian

indicators.note: the island lets the other letters in

parts.note: the Isle of Man
lay means amateur, not of a profession

explanation.surface: An island lets in an amateur from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malayan comes from Malaya, now part of Malaysia, in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Disembark and take a tumble where one leaves the sea

parts.note: to land is to come ashore
to fall is to take a tumble

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles getting off a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfall is the arrival at land at the end of a sea voyage.

clue.text: Light shawl worn if going up to central Manchuria

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means read from bottom to top
central means the middle letters of Manchuria

explanation.surface: A light wrap is worn when climbing into northern China.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular lace scarf worn round a woman's neck.

clue.text: A rookie follows the old soldiers and becomes a rogue

indicators.note: the rookie comes after the soldiers

parts.note: RASC was the Royal Army Service Corps, a former British Army unit
L stands for learner, a novice

explanation.surface: A new recruit joins veteran troops and turns bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous scoundrel.

clue.text: It's material when a sycophant turns tail

indicators.note: the tail of the word, its final two letters, is turned around

parts.note: a creep is a fawning toady

explanation.surface: A crawler flees, and it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' looks like running away, but reverses the last two letters of CREEP, giving PE for EP.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled fabric.

clue.text: United group put politician in gaol

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison
L is a Liberal

explanation.surface: A political faction locks up a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a close-knit family group bound by kinship.

clue.text: It goes to and fro serving the city

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A commuter travels back and forth for the municipality.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town.

clue.text: Thoroughly modern girl stocking new lines in headgear

indicators.note: the girl holds the other letter inside, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: Thoroughly Modern Millie is a 1967 film musical
N is new
RY is railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A trendy girl keeps new styles of hats in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Millinery is women's hats as a trade or collective goods.

clue.text: Gent erupting violently on the golf-course

indicators.note: violently signals the letters of gent erupting are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A golfer loses his temper on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: The putting green is the smooth turf round each hole, found on a golf course.
